newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban accuse Russia of scaremongering in C.Asia.
newsitem.headline: Taleban accuse Russia of scaremongering in C.Asia.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban militia on Thursday accused Russia of scaremongering to preserve their influence in the former Soviet republics of Central Asia.

"Russia has told (the Central Asian) states that the Taleban is a danger to them so they would ask for Russian help and a Russian military presence in their countries," Information Minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told Reuters on Thursday.
"We have declared in the past to the Central Asian republics, and we wish to repeat, that we have no intention of interfering in the affairs of any other country," he added.
Mutaqi was responding to reports of a meeting on Wednesday between the defence ministers of Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan in the Uzbek capital Tashkent.
According to a report by the Interfax news agency, the ministers agreed on a coordinated reaction if the Taleban moved close to the border that Afghanistan shares with Uzbekistan and Tajikistan.

"Interfax learnt from a competent source that that meeting had worked out concrete and coordinated actions which would serve as an adequate reaction to the possibility of the military units of the Taleban moving close to the southern borders of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)," said the report.

Most of the border between Afghanistan and the former Soviet Union is controlled by the anti-Taleban alliance led by General Abdul Rashid Dostum, himself a former military commander of the Afghan communist regime.
The only CIS Central Asian state that shares a border with Taleban-controlled territory, Turkmenistan, did not attend the defence ministers' conference.
